samples.summary: Design doc overstates the new guarantee: the tree-side refusal is gated behind a model-side precondition, so some replacing writes still delete rows they never read
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md now states the incremental replacing writers carry the refusal "checked against the rows the CRDT actually holds under the range they are about to overwrite (`treeHasTruncatedRows`)". In code the tree check only runs when the *new model* already trips `hasTableAtNestingCap`: `setHeader` (line 1015: `if (header && hadHeader && hasTableAtNestingCap(header.blocks, 0))`), `setFooter` (line 1060), `updateBlock` (line ~1822) and `updateTableCell` (line ~3006). A replacement whose model no longer contains a table at the cap — e.g. a header rebuilt from content in which the truncated table was removed or never round-tripped — skips `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` entirely and `editByPath([0],[1],node)` still replicates the deletion of a peer's rows. The doc describes an unconditional tree-side guarantee; the implementation is a heuristic fast path. Either narrow the doc wording or move the gate.

samples.summary: The whole-document "refuse the edit" policy is extended to hot incremental writers with no caller-side handling, so an ordinary gesture can throw mid-edit
samples.evidence: `writeFullDocument` throwing was justified in docs-nested-tables.md as a rare, deliberate whole-tree rewrite where "the one thing lost is the edit, not the document". `updateBlock` and `updateTableCell` are reached from ordinary gestures — e.g. `pasteTableCells` in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts calls `normalizeTableMerges(td)` then `this.doc.updateBlockDirect(tableBlockId, tableBlock)` → `store.updateBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:793). The new throw fires after the caller has already mutated its local `Block`/`tableData` object, so the local model and the CRDT diverge and the exception escapes the input handler; I found no catch/user-facing error path for `truncatedRowsError()` anywhere in the frontend. Reachable only on a document a peer wrote past the cap, hence minor, but the approach (throw) fits a save-time path better than a keystroke-adjacent one.

samples.summary: The merge-expansion budget policy this delta redefines (paint-only bound, unbounded on every acting path including local delete/copy/cut) is recorded only in code comments, not in any design doc
samples.evidence: `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` and the newly narrowed contract — `normalizeCellRange`/`normalizeRange` now default to `Infinity` and only `computeSelectionRects` passes a budget — is a policy about peer-written data and hang risk, the same class of rule `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` gets a documented section for in docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md. This delta materially widens the unbounded surface: `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (5 call sites in text-editor.ts) now runs a superlinear fixed-point expansion over a table whose row count is a peer's to choose, on the local delete/copy/cut gestures. Nothing in docs/design records that trade-off.

samples.summary: Scope creep relative to the originating issue (#1049): CRDT write-refusal machinery and a second paste-nesting cap are unrelated to the stated outcome
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md scopes the change to (1) resolving nested tables in `normalizeRange` so read-time merge expansion runs, (2) shift+click building a `tableCellRange`, (3) the corresponding tests. This delta adds `treeHasTruncatedRows`/`assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` and refusals on `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `setHeader`, `setFooter`, plus `capTableCellsNesting` on the `pasteTableCells` path — nesting-cap hardening that neither the issue's outcome nor its acceptance criteria ask for, and that changes write-path behaviour (new throws) well outside the selection/merge-paint bug. Worth splitting out so the #1049 fix can be judged and reverted independently.

searchedFor: grep capTableNesting|tableNestingDepth across repo (only editor.ts:4232, document.ts:925, text-editor.ts:4568)
finding.summary: The design doc section this change adds asserts "**Producers** never create one past it: … paste drops the tables in a fragment that would (`capTableNesting`, counted against the paste target's own depth)" (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:293-296), but only ONE of the two paste branches is capped. `handlePaste` dispatches to `insertBlocks` (capped at text-editor.ts:4568) or to `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4698), and the cell-range branch clones the clipboard `TableCell[][]` straight into the target cells (`td.rows[targetRow].cells[targetCol] = cloned`, line 4749) with no depth check at all. A clipboard cell payload may legally carry nested tables (the sanitizer's own `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH` = 8 permits them, clipboard.ts:72), so pasting such cells into a cell already ~25 tables deep produces exactly the state the cap exists to prevent — and since `buildBlockNode` then writes any table at/past the cap with `children: []`, the pasted rows are silently dropped into the CRDT rather than refused. The stated invariant therefore does not hold for the cell-rectangle paste, which is the paste path most likely to carry tables.
finding.evidence: text-editor.ts:4740-4751 copies cells with `cloneTableCells` and no `capTableNesting` / `tableNestingDepth` call; the only capped call site is line 4568 inside `insertBlocks`.

verdict.reason: The cell-rectangle paste branch IS depth-capped, by a sibling helper named `capTableCellsNesting` — a name that does not contain the substring `capTableNesting`, which is why the reviewer's greps came up empty. `pasteTableCells` computes `cellBaseDepth = this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) + (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` (text-editor.ts:4719-4720) and applies `capTableCellsNesting(cloneTableCells([[cells[r][c]]]), cellBaseDepth)` on BOTH sub-branches before writing: the new-table branch at 4730-4734 and the in-table branch at 4765-4769. `capTableCellsNesting` (clipboard.ts:462-473) delegates per cell to the very same `capTableNesting` (clipboard.ts:429-447) that `insertBlocks` uses at text-editor.ts:4568. The finding's quoted evidence is additionally inaccurate: line 4749 is `const tableBlockId = cellInfo.tableBlockId;`, and the actual cell assignment (4769) assigns the capped clone. The design-doc sentence quoted even names both paths explicitly (docs-nested-tables.md:295-296), and tests cover the second writer (table-nesting.test.ts:11,193). The asserted invariant holds.
